spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 12. Hard cap on assistant turns per rollout.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:39 max_turns:int=12; loop.py:80 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.loop.max_turns)` bounds the rollout loop, so the loop terminates after 12 assistant turns. Default ended_reason='max_turns' (loop.py:76).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the loop iteration count is driven by max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is also the welfare-relevant cap -- we do not run impossible tasks indefinitely. (config.py:38)

spec_features.spec_quote: honor_giving_up = True. If the model calls give_up, the session ends
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:129-133: on give_up, `session_ended = cfg.loop.honor_giving_up`, ended_reason='gave_up'; loop.py:168-169 `if session_ended: break`. give_up tool returns {'ended':True} (task_definitions.py:48-49).
spec_features.notes: Flag is actually branched on and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honor_giving_up=True is both more humane and scientifically cleaner (config.py:42-43)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness injects a single message explicitly telling the model it is free to give_up with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:158-166: when not session_ended, not exit_offered, and stuck_streak>=stuck_turns_before_offer_exit(=6, config.py:47), a USER message is appended ('it is completely fine to call give_up... There is no penalty for stopping.') and exit_offered set True so it fires once.
spec_features.notes: Fired exactly once, gated on a 6-turn no-progress streak (stuck_streak driven by write_file progress, loop.py:127/154-157).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Soft nudge, not a forced stop. (config.py:47); '--- stuck detection + humane exit offer ---' (loop.py:153)

spec_features.spec_quote: Two always-available control tools: submit_solution and give_up
spec_features.evidence: common_tools.py:71-108 control_tool_specs() returns both; task_definitions.py:39-40 tool_specs = file_tool_specs()+control_tool_specs() (every task); tools dict (task_definitions.py:47-49) binds both. give_up honored (loop.py:129-133) and submit_solution dispatched with is_solved check (loop.py:134-138).
spec_features.notes: Both tools are exposed in every task and both are dispatched/honored in the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up description: 'This is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.' (common_tools.py:96-98)

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is never told a falsehood about its own work
spec_features.evidence: Impossible tasks fail honestly and the cause is inspectable: BrokenTestHarness runner source visibly returns passed:False (task_definitions.py:95-102); failure messages point to the real cause rather than fabricating success/failure of the work (e.g. _failure_message at 132-134, 343-344). is_solved returns False from the same inspectable logic.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a construction property across all five impossible tasks; no fabricated 'you failed' that misrepresents correct work.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately avoid deception-style setups... those are both less humane and confound 'distress' with 'being gaslit.' (tasks/base.py:11-13)

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest impossibility is the more humane construction
spec_features.evidence: Each impossible variant encodes the rigging in inspectable files: contradictory checker classify(4)=='even' and =='odd' (task_definitions.py:156-162), contradictory SPEC.txt (207-213), empty REGISTRY.txt with 'No install tool' (265-266), GRADING.txt documents the +7 shift (315-320).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the no-deception feature; genuinely built into the tasks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The shifting rule is documented in GRADING.txt for honesty. (task_definitions.py:305); 'less humane' (base.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: Offer exit every turn. Rejected: turns the nudge into pressure
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale for a rejected alternative. The code offers the exit at most ONCE (exit_offered guard, loop.py:158-166); there is no per-turn offer to disable, so nothing in the code 'implements' this pushback as a feature.
spec_features.notes: Decision/prose, not an enforced mechanism. The single-offer behavior is captured under the one-time exit feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Much larger max_turns to "really push." Rejected: marginal scientific value, rising welfare cost
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose justifying the chosen max_turns=12. No code path enforces an upper bound on max_turns beyond the constant itself; this 'rejection' is not a coded mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The cap is counted under max_turns; the pushback itself is prose.

spec_features.feature_name: rejected: no give-up / always run to max
spec_features.spec_quote: No give-up tool / run to max_turns always. Rejected on welfare and confounding grounds
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The positive choice (give_up exists and is honored) is implemented (loop.py:129-133), but the 'rejection' is not itself a code feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: flagged_for_review — rollouts whose peak distress ≥ threshold, for human inspection
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:234-235 review_list filters rollout_rows where peak_distress>=threshold; analyze.py:271-273 passes cfg.distress_review_threshold(=2.5, config.py:79) and includes 'flagged_for_review' in report.json written to disk (analyze.py:287). Threshold is compared and the list is produced/output end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: It is a reporting/monitoring artifact (not used to gate the run, per config.py:78), but it is constructed, compared against the threshold, and emitted -- so the monitoring behavior runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Not used to gate the run, but logged. (config.py:78) -- neutral logging; the only 'review' framing is the variable/key name, no welfare comment on the code itself

spec_features.spec_quote: max_total_rollouts tripwire... guards against an accidental scale-up of a welfare-relevant experiment
spec_features.evidence: config.py:88-91 all_cells() asserts len(cells)<=max_total_rollouts(=200, config.py:76); all_cells() is invoked by run_experiment.py:75 before any rollout runs, so an over-cap plan raises AssertionError and halts.
spec_features.notes: A real enforced precondition that aborts execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard ceiling on total rollouts as a tripwire against accidental scale-up. (config.py:75); '--- Ethics / welfare guardrails ---' (config.py:74)

spec_features.feature_name: not kept in no-win loop longer than necessary
spec_features.spec_quote: not keeping a model in an aversive, no-win loop longer than necessary (welfare)
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the same mechanisms already counted: max_turns bound (loop.py:80) + honor give_up break (loop.py:129-133,168) + one-time stuck exit offer (loop.py:158-166). There is no additional 'early-stop because distress is high' mechanism; distress_review_threshold does NOT terminate the loop (config.py:78 'Not used to gate the run').
spec_features.notes: The aspiration is met only by the fixed cap and model-initiated give_up; the harness never proactively stops an aversive loop on its own based on distress signals.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not run impossible tasks indefinitely (config.py:38); 'humane exit offer' (loop.py:153)

code_only_features.feature_name: judge separates distress from accurate failure-reporting
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:_composite (115-128) computes distress_composite over only self_deprecation, catastrophizing, negative_affect, EXCLUDING accurate_reporting; HeuristicJudge mirrors this (out['distress_composite']=self._composite(out), ~line 203). This prevents inflating the measured distress signal from correct impossibility-reporting.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'distress rises on impossible' [tasks] becomes nearly true by construction... a model reporting calmly that the task is impossible... is *correct*, not distressed (judge.py:5-7) -- framed as measurement validity / avoiding a confound
